memory_candidates.content: When a verification gate includes a negative test ('the defect recorder emits NO event on a clean run'), check the detector's own trigger conditions before concluding the system is healthy or unhealthy. A live defect in the detection path can make the negative test structurally unpassable for reasons unrelated to the system under test. Concrete instance: hooks/validate-handoff-location.sh matches handoff paths with a fixed-position [0-9]{3} task-directory regex and, on a non-match, both exits 2 and calls system-defect-record.sh --defect-class HANDOFF_MISLOCATED. Once specs/state.json's next_project_number crossed 1000, every new task became 4-digit, so every such task's handoff write emits a spurious defect event. Any acceptance criterion asserting 'no defect events on a clean run' is therefore unpassable until that regex is widened -- the gate is BLOCKED, not FAILING. Generalization: a gate whose pass condition depends on a detector's silence inherits every one of that detector's false-positive modes.
